statement: Erdos 273 witness search by SAT: after the exact parity split (every modulus p-1, p>=5, is even), the problem is equivalent to H = {(p-1)/2 : p prime, p>=5} containing TWO DISJOINT distinct-moduli covering systems of Z. Selfridge's p>=3 example supplies one legal half (divisors of 180 in H: {2,3,5,6,9,15,18,20,30,36,90}, moduli p-1 for p in {5,7,11,13,19,31,37,41,61,73,181}). Search: CNF-encode 'cover Z/N with distinct moduli from H minus the moduli already used by the first half, all dividing N', ladder N = 3960, 7920, 27720, 55440, 110880; also allow re-choosing the first half. A SAT witness is re-verified by an independent exact covering check, then kernel-verified by a parity-split Lean file (decide per residue class).
definition_source: Erdos & Graham 1980, Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory (problem 273 on erdosproblems.com, reference [ErGr80]); covering systems per Erdos 1950 / Selfridge; canonical Lean statement in oracle/acquisition/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/273.lean (StrictCoveringSystem) - the stage-1 statement firewall must confirm the exact predicate (distinct moduli, all of the form p-1 with p>=5 prime, finite) before any witness is called a close.
asked_question: Close a canonical open Erdos problem (operator: the bar). Pool scans A and B ranked 273 the pool's one session-scale ladder target; pricing 2026-09-02 found it OPEN with no refutation available (Filaseta-Kalogirou 2024 needs minimum modulus > 4; ours is exactly 4).
proxy_reason: SAT over a ladder of N proves existence only if it finds a witness; UNSAT at every rung is a bounded nonexistence fact (no covering with lcm dividing the tested N), never closure of the negative branch - every outcome line states this.
novel_if: Any witness resolves Erdos 273 affirmatively (open since 1980, no progress recorded). A ladder of UNSAT rungs is the first quantitative bound on the problem, recorded as COMPUTATION.
